title: thaspium aureum var. trifoliatum
intro: Thaspium aureum var. trifoliatum, commonly known as Western meadow rue, is a perennial herb native to North America, characterized by its yellowish-green foliage and clusters of small, white flowers. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to reduce pain, improve digestion, and boost the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Western meadow rue include its ability to act as a diuretic, a diaphoretic, and a mild expectorant, making it useful for treating conditions such as urinary tract infections, fever, and bronchitis. The bioactive constituents of Western meadow rue include sesquiterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
